prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (non-ideological)

Economy and business
- Responsible public finances; focus tax changes on a one-off windfall tax on oil and gas super-profits, reversing bank tax cuts, increasing the Digital Services Tax to 6%, fairer capital gains tax, and a 4% levy on FTSE-100 share buybacks.
- Industrial strategy centred on green infrastructure, renewables, digital and biosciences; expand the British Business Bank.
- Abolish business rates and replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy; curb late payments; promote employee ownership; circular-economy measures.
- AI framework to promote innovation, transparency and accountability; digital literacy target and clearer consumer T&Cs.
- Skills: replace the apprenticeship levy with a flexible skills levy; guarantee apprentices at least the National Minimum Wage; £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants for adults (aim to rise to £10,000).

Energy and climate
- Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; rooftop solar expansion; maintain fracking ban and ban new coal mines.
- Ten-year Home Energy Upgrade (free insulation and heat pumps for low-income homes); social energy tariff; decouple electricity prices from gas.
- Expand storage (green hydrogen, batteries, pumped storage); grid upgrades; more interconnectors; enable community energy and local grids.
- Associate UK ETS with the EU ETS; Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism; climate-aligned financial regulation.

Health and social care
- Right to see a GP within seven days (24 hours if urgent), with 8,000 more GPs; 24/7 booking; greater role for pharmacists and nurses.
- NHS dentistry access for urgent care; reform dental contracts; prevention measures (school toothbrushing).
- Mental health hubs for young people; regular mental health check-ups; end out-of-area placements; more talking therapies; perinatal support.
- Cancer: 100% start treatment within 62 days; replace ageing radiotherapy; more cancer nurses; research act; faster approvals.
- Public health: vape restrictions and single-use ban; extend soft drinks levy; clean air law; tobacco profits levy.
- Social care: free personal care; Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hour); Royal College of Care Workers; paid carer’s leave and guaranteed respite; National Care Agency and national standards.

Education and families
- A qualified mental health professional in every school; per‑pupil funding increases above inflation; repair schools; tutoring for disadvantaged pupils.
- Early years: extra five free hours for disadvantaged 3–4 year‑olds; triple Early Years Pupil Premium; restore university maintenance grants.
- Curriculum and assessment reform; strengthen SEND support; arts in EBacc; Young People’s Premium (16–18); rejoin Erasmus+.
- Extend free school meals to all children in poverty; overhaul parental leave: double Statutory Maternity and Shared Parental Pay, higher paternity pay, day-one rights, self‑employed included.

Housing and communities
- Build 380,000 homes/year, including 150,000 social homes; 10 new garden cities; faster brownfield use; “use‑it‑or‑lose‑it” permissions.
- Abolish leasehold; cap ground rents; ban no‑fault evictions; default three‑year tenancies; national landlord register; powers to end Right to Buy locally.
- End rough sleeping; rent-to-own for social housing; remove dangerous cladding.
- Local government: multi‑year funding settlements; powers over second homes/short lets; nationwide gigabit broadband.

Crime and justice
- Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance for burglaries; Online Crime Agency; Hillsborough Law.
- Halve time from offence to sentencing; tackle court backlogs; public health approach to youth violence; stronger anti-fraud protections.
- Modern slavery: stronger enforcement authority and civil remedies.

Environment and farming
- New regulator for water; end sewage discharges; public-benefit company model; binding nature targets (“double nature” by 2050); 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act.
- Deposit return scheme; phase out non‑recyclable single‑use plastics; peatland and blue carbon restoration.
- Environmental Land Management accelerated and +£1bn/year; high standards in trade; veterinary and plant health agreements with the EU.

Transport
- Restore 2030 zero‑emission sales requirement; expand EV charging; cut VAT on public charging to 5%; reintroduce plug‑in grant.
- Freeze rail fares; new Railway Agency; major rail electrification; Northern Powerhouse Rail; bus franchising powers; £2 fare cap maintained; national active travel strategy.
- Reform flight taxes toward frequent flyers; restrict short domestic flights where rail <2.5 hours (with exceptions).

Immigration and asylum
- Move work/student visa policy out of the Home Office; flexible, sector‑led work visa system; exempt NHS/care from skills charge; expand Youth Mobility.
- Scrap Rwanda plan; three‑month service standard for asylum decisions; allow work after 3 months; expand safe and legal routes; limit detention (no children; 28‑day cap for adults).
- Simplify rules; reverse family visa threshold rise; secure rights for EU citizens; implement Windrush reforms; firewall public services from immigration enforcement.

Rights, democracy, defence and international
- Proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councils; cap donations; Lords reform; votes at 16; written federal constitution and devolution.
- Human Rights Act/ECHR upheld; ban conversion practices; digital rights and biometric safeguards; gender recognition reform; disability employment support.
- Defence spending rising toward 2.5% GDP; reverse Army cuts; improve housing and support for personnel; stricter arms export controls.
- Foreign policy: rebuild EU ties via phased roadmap (including vet/plant health deals; aim to join Single Market longer term); support Ukraine (including seize Russian assets); restore ODA to 0.7% with a dedicated department; ceasefire and two‑state approach in Israel‑Palestine; recognise Palestine.
